Atlanta · The Southeast · The Caribbean

Regional Indian & global catering for the moments that matter.

Home-style North Indian cooking from Chef Archna Becker,

for weddings, offices, and celebrations.
Bhojanic catering avaIlble in atlanta, The southeast, and The CARIBBEAN

Archna Malhotra Becker is the visionary behind Bhojanic, one of

Atlanta’s most celebrated Indian restaurants. With over 25 years of

experience, she has redefined the Indian dining scene, earning

numerous accolades, including multiple “Best Indian Restaurant”

awards from Creative Loafing, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution, and

Atlanta Magazine. In 2011, Atlanta Magazine recognized Bhojanic as

one of the city’s 50 Best Restaurants.Archna’s passion for food

began in India, where she learned traditional home-style cooking

from her grandmother. After moving to the U.S. at age 11, her

entrepreneurial spirit led her to convince her parents to help launch

Atlanta North Indian Cuisine (ANIC), a catering business that gained

a stellar reputation, catering high-profile events and securing

contracts with Grammy-winning artists.

Building on that success, Archna opened Bhojanic, known for its

authentic, home-style Indian cuisine served as full meals and

tapas-style small plates. The brand expanded to multiple locations,

including Bhojanic Buckhead in 2013, Georgia Tech and Emory in

2016, and the launch of the Bhojanic Food Truck in 2015. In 2020,

she introduced Tandoori Pizza & Wing Co., a modern twist on Indian

flavors that has since grown into multiple locations.

In 2025, Archna is expanding to Evergreen, Colorado, with The

Yellow House 1924, an experiential event space dedicated to supper

clubs, pop-ups, and immersive cooking classes. A recognized leader

in the restaurant industry, she has served on the board of the

Georgia Restaurant Association and has been a board member of

the National Restaurant Association since 2020. She was also

nominated for Restaurateur of the Year in 2013.

Beyond her restaurants, Archna has made national television

appearances, been a featured guest chef on cruises and destination

weddings, and continues to push the boundaries of Indian cuisine in

innovative and unexpected ways.

/india-food-tour.title: India Food Tour — bhojanic
blocks:
𑁍 Spice Route 𑁍
Chef Archna’s Culinary Journey Through India

Winter 2028

A 15-day exploration of North and South India, combining unforgettable culinary experiences with iconic sights—from bustling markets and spice-laden kitchens to majestic forts, temples, and tranquil backwaters.’

𑁍
ABOUT THIS JOURNEY

This is a collaborative venture between Chef Archna Becker and Rebecca Liebeskind, created from a shared passion for culture, hospitality, and a deep connection to India.

Led by Chef Archna Becker, this culinary and cultural experience offers an in-depth exploration of the diverse food traditions of North and South India. With decades of experience as a chef, restaurateur, and cultural ambassador, Archna brings a unique perspective—born in India, raised in the U.S., and professionally trained in both worlds. Her approach bridges tradition and innovation, offering participants an immersive and deeply personal window into Indian cuisine.

Rebecca brings over 15 years of experience in experiential travel planning, with a focus on crafting intentional, sensory-rich journeys throughout India. Her love for Indian food and culture began during her years working at Bhojanic, where she and Archna first met. That experience sparked a lasting connection to the stories behind the cuisine—and a passion for sharing those stories through curated, meaningful travel experiences.

To bring this vision to life, Archna and Rebecca are partnering with a bespoke local Indian travel agency that shares their values of authenticity, care, and thoughtful design. Together, they are crafting a journey that goes beyond sightseeing—offering travelers profound encounters with India’s culinary heritage, cultural richness, and human stories.

𑁍
What You’ll Experience

The itinerary is thoughtfully designed to showcase the richness and variety of Indian cuisine across regions. You'll explore:

✺ Delhi for its dynamic street food scene and historic spice markets

✺ Rajasthan for royal culinary traditions and desert hospitality

✺ Kerala for coastal cuisine, Ayurvedic food practices, and backwater living

Along the way, you'll enjoy guided market visits, cooking demonstrations, curated meals in local homes and restaurants, and meaningful cultural excursions.

This is not a standard food tour. It’s an immersive, expertly guided experience designed to connect you to India’s culinary heritage through the lens of a seasoned chef who knows it intimately.

What You Can Expect:

✺ A thoughtfully curated itinerary through India’s most iconic and diverse culinary regions

✺ Guided food tours through vibrant markets, street vendors, and hidden local favorites

✺ Hands-on cooking sessions with regional chefs, home cooks, and culinary artisans

✺ Boutique and heritage accommodations that blend comfort, elegance, and cultural character

✺ A balanced pace designed for immersion—allowing time to explore, reflect, and savor

✺ Intimate meals, shared stories, and personal insights from Chef Archna throughout the journey

✺ Private, comfortable transportation to ensure a seamless and relaxed travel experience

𑁍 About Chef Archna

Archna Becker is the chef and visionary behind Bhojanic. Born in India, raised in the U.S., and rooted in the flavors of both, she offers more than recipes — she offers relationship. To ingredients, to stories, and to the invisible threads that tie generations together.

This journey is the one she’s dreamed of leading: returning to India not just as a visitor, but as a bridge.

𑁍 LIMITED CAPACITY

Chef Archna’s Spice Route is an intentionally intimate experience.
Spaces are limited to allow for presence, connection, and immersion.

𑁍 The Route

This Journey Follows the Spices

From the vibrant markets of the North to the lush hills of the South, every stop is a celebration of India’s regional flavors, timeless traditions, and sensory richness.

✺ Delhi
 Begin in India’s bustling capital with bold street food, iconic spice bazaars, and Mughal-inspired cuisine. Wander through Chandni Chowk, savor sizzling kebabs, and explore the layered flavors that define North Indian cooking.

✺ Agra
 Stand before the Taj Mahal, then dive into Agra’s Mughal culinary legacy—featuring rich curries, aromatic biryanis, and delicate sweets shaped by royal influence.

✺ Udaipur
 In the romantic City of Lakes, enjoy serene beauty and warm Rajasthani hospitality. Visit vibrant markets, explore traditional vegetarian cuisine, and share meals in a heritage home surrounded by palace views and quiet hills.

✺ Fort Kochi
 Arrive in Kerala through this coastal spice port. Taste fresh seafood, walk the historic streets shaped by traders and settlers, and enjoy dishes infused with coconut, curry leaf, and centuries of culinary exchange.

✺ Munnar
 In the cool hills of tea and spice country, stroll through lush plantations, visit cardamom and pepper farms, and learn how the land itself shapes Kerala’s cuisine.

✺ Alleppey
 Unwind on a private houseboat gliding through Kerala’s backwaters. Cook with local ingredients onboard, enjoy traditional Kerala meals, and take in the rhythms of daily life along the canals.

Taste the Soul of India with Chef Archna Becker

Embark on a 15-day culinary journey through Delhi, Agra, Rajasthan, and Kerala with renowned Chef Archna Becker. Explore India’s rich flavors, vibrant culture, and heartfelt traditions through food, connection, and unforgettable experiences.

𑁍 View the Itinerary

Want a closer look at what’s in store?

Download the full itinerary and explore the details of this curated experience — from daily destinations to immersive culinary moments.

DEAR ARCHNA,

"By the way, I don't know if I have told you this… I tell all my friends and clients that you are the only Indian Restaurant in Atlanta worth going to. There are so many now, but none of them surpass your quality and style."

-Chitra

"Ram and I want to thank you on behalf of the entire wedding party and all the guests for dinner on June 23rd 2007. The menu selection was perfect. Thank you for helping us, your service was out of this world. You far exceeded our expectations. The compliments started prior to dinner when cocktails were served, we got so many inquiries on who did the catering for us. Compliments continued all through dinner. If I had to pick one favorite dish, I would be at a loss, every bite was mouth watering. From the kebabs and Chicken 65 for cocktails to the Tikka Masala during dinner… and oh the Rusmalai… divine. We are thankful to you and your staff for being so cooperative and on time, delivering in a professional manner and at the right temperature. It makes all the difference. Just so you know, we had guests from Germany, Japan, Spain, India, and New York, and they made comments such as "this is the best indian food we have ever had, it was so tender is just melted in
my mouth" and 'the best Rusmalai ever.'"

-Uma

"A big thank you for the wonderful arrangements for our event on May 22nd. I think everyone had a great time. The food of course was delicious, and up to everyone's expectation. As you well know, your cooking has developed a great name in the community, and I am quite certain that news about this Sat. will definitely add to your reputation. Poonam and Surendraji are wonderful, and it was a pleasure having them around as well. My husband was very impressed with the positive energy that you yourself had all evening."

-Shabnam

"I just wanted to let you know that your team did a fabulous job with the catering order. Eveyone had nothing but good things to say about the quality & quantity of the food that you supplied. Once again you did a superb job. For me personally what I liked best was the chicken tikka masala, bhindi, gulabjamun and of course the rasmalai."

-Dilip Jain

Its been some time since we last spoke. Once again I would like to thank you for the fantastic service that you provided for my pooja event. The food was delicious, especially the Halwa and the desserts. All my guests were complimenting the  food. Also, the quantity was perfect, in fact we had some leftovers which we enjoyed eating in the next few days after the pooja. I will definitely recommend your restaurant to all my friends and relatives.

-Priya Sahetiya

I want to personally thank Bhojanic for the exceptional service and care you and your staff provided when my wife and I hosted Shashi Tharoor at Emory University when he delivered the Annual Sheth Lecture on Indian Studies. At a very short
notice, you were able to manage the event in the midst of one of the busiest weekends in Atlanta. I am deeply grateful for your personal commitment and care in making the event successful and enjoyable.

-Jagdish N. Sheth, Ph.D.

"Our event was a great success. Everybody had a wonderful time and loved the food. Your food was good in quality and adequate in quantity. Thank you!"

-Nayantara Shah

"The food at dinner was absolutely incredible and Justin & Yasmeen were totally FANTASTIC. Thank you for delivering way above expectations."

-Jaspal Bhasin

"I wanted to send an email of huge thanks to you and the staff at the Cooks Warehouse.  Our company party was talked about for days following this event.  The theme of an Iron Chef competition inspired my team to get competitive and do what they love most that is cooking. Who would have guessed that cooking was so popular but we could not have planned any better. All of my wannabee chef's got to show their stuff.

I think we had it all, those who played it safe and followed the recipe, those who were innovative and could care less about the recipe and of course those who set out to sabotage the other teams.  Between the drama, theatre and the wonderful food and wine it was clear that the entertainment value was outstanding and will not be forgotten.

We would all like to express that we appreciate you letting us be ourselves and free to experiment. I am certain we will be doing another of these events in the future. Also,  thank you for hosting this event making it fun and the most memorable celebration we could experience."

-Nacine Bryson

Associate Partner, IBM Global Business Services

/curry-jam-karl-denson.title: Curry Jam Karl Denson — bhojanic
blocks: JAM CRUISE #CURRYjam RECIPES

INGREDIENTS
4 tbsp Oil (Canola or Vegetable)

2 cups diced yellow onion

1 lb Baby Okra cut lengthwise 

1 ½  tsp Mango Powder

1 ½ tsp Coriander, ground

1 tsp Cumin, ground

1 ½  tsp Fennel Seed, ground

1 ½ tsp Turmeric

1 ½ to 2 tsp salt, to taste

3/4 tsp to 1 tsp of cayenne, to taste

Chopped cilantro leaves

STEP 1
Cut the okra on both ends and cut into ½” pieces. You can also split them down the middle. Do not use thick pieces of okra with big seeds. Baby okra works the best for this recipe.  

STEP 2
Heat the oil in a heavy bottom pan and sauté the onions until caramelized and golden brown. Usually takes 8-10 minutes on medium heat.

STEP 3
Add the okra and sprinkle with the mango powder. Cook together till the okra is bright green.

STEP 4
Add the other dry ingredients and cook on low heat till the okra is tender. It will will turn a darker color and will shrink in size. Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve with naan or rice.

/curry-jam-eddie-roberts.title: Curry Jam Eddie Roberts — bhojanic
blocks: JAM CRUISE #CURRYjam RECIPES

STEP 1
Boil the potatoes unpeeled and washed until knife tender. Once cool, peel and cut into small cubes.

STEP 2
Heat the oil in a heavy bottom wok shaped pan over medium heat for 30 seconds. Add the bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cloves, cardamom, and cumin seeds. Wait until they sizzle and you smell them.

STEP 3
Add the ginger and garlic paste. Cook for a few minutes until caramelized. Add the onion and cook until caramelized. Now add the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes.

STEP 4
Add the cooked potatoes and stir together, and add the spinach leaves and the salt, cayenne, turmeric, and ground coriander. Cover and cook on low heat for 10-15 minutes. If the bottom of the pan starts sticking, add a tablespoon of water and scrape the bottom. Cover and cook on low heat till everything is incorporated. Adjust the salt to taste. Serve with rice or naan bread.

INGREDIENTS

1 tsp minced fresh garlic

1 tsp minced ground ginger

1 medium onion sliced thin

2 ½ tablespoon canola or vegetable oil

1 cinnamon stick

½ teaspoon cumin seeds

3 cardamom pods

2 bay leafs

1-4 tablespoon water

3 cloves whole

½ teaspoon turmeric

1 ½ tsp. ground coriander

3 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes

1- 1 ¼ teaspoon salt or to taste

½ teaspoon cayenne pepper 

¼ cup tomato puree (can) -or-
You can substitute diced tomato (½ cup)

14 oz. fresh spinach, finely chopped

/curry-jam-roosevelt-collier.title: Curry Jam Roosevelt Collier — bhojanic
blocks: JAM CRUISE #CURRYjam RECIPES

INGREDIENTS
WINGS
3 pounds chicken wings

2 tsp salt

⅛ cup lemon juice

1 ¼ cups plain yogurt

1 tsp ginger paste

1 tsp garlic paste

3 tsp Tandoori Masala (store bought) 

1 tsp cayenne pepper

2 tsp paprika

2 tbsp Canola oil

INGREDIENTS
MANGO CHILI SAUCE

1 cup Major Grey’s Mango chutney

¼ cup Sriracha hot sauce or to your heat level

2 tbsp lemon juice

WINGS
STEP 1
Combine the yogurt, lemon juice, ginger, garlic, oil, and all the dry spices. Add the chicken and coat evenly.  Marinate the chicken for 6-24 hours, the longer the better.

STEP 2
Bake in oven (use Convection setting is available) on 350 degrees until chicken is almost cooked (time varies due to wing size but generally 30-40 minutes).

STEP 3
To finish put the oven on 500 degrees convection and cook the wings till they get a char color. You can also fry the wings after the initial cooking time. You will fry them on 350 degrees till you see a little char.

The last way to cook them is on the outdoor grill.  That you can do from raw on 350 degrees till you see some burnt ends. Once the wings are fully cooked, toss them with the sauce and garnish with scallions.

MANGO CHILI WING SAUCE
STEP 1
Cook all the above ingredients on medium heat until all the ingredients are incorporated.

STEP 2
Use a blender to smooth out the sauce.

STEP 3
Put wings and sauce in a bowl, toss to coat and serve.

/curry-jam-dj-logic.title: Curry Jam DJ Logic — bhojanic
blocks: JAM CRUISE #CURRYjam RECIPES

INGREDIENTS

2 pounds chicken thighs cut into pieces (fat removed)

6 Tbsp. oil

2 Cups ground onion pulp

1½ tbsp ground ginger

1 tbsp ground garlic

¾ cup plain yogurt

¼ cup tomato puree (Canned)

1-2 cups water

1 tsp cumin seed

6 whole cardamom pods

6 whole cloves

2 medium cinnamon sticks

2-2½    tsp. salt

1-1½  tsp. cayenne

2 tsp Coriander ground

¾ tsp Turmeric

¼ tsp ground cardamom

Chopped Cilantro for garnish

STEP 1
In a heavy bottom pan, heat the oil on medium heat and add cumin seed, whole cloves, whole cardamom, and cinnamon sticks. Once they sizzle and you can smell the spices, add the ginger and garlic.  Cook for 30 seconds to a minute until the mix is golden brown.

STEP 2
Add the onions and cook until the mix is golden brown. Then add the chicken and cook together until the chicken is nicely coated.  

STEP 3
Next add the ground spices including coriander, cayenne, turmeric, and salt.  Cook the meat for additional 10-15 minutes until tender. Then add the tomato puree and yogurt.  Cook for 5-7 minutes and then add water. Simmer for 15 to 30 minutes. When the fat ends up floating at the top, you know it is ready.  

STEP 4
Check the salt and garnish with chopped cilantro. Serve with rice or flatbread.  You can substitute any meat with this recipe but will need to adjust cooking time accordingly.  Lamb and Goat take two to three times longer to get tender than chicken.
